title: Implement model changelog generator worker (consume change-events -> draft release notes -> docs publish link)
author: Michael Nguyen
release_notes: Internal: Adds generator worker to produce customer-safe model release note drafts from registry change-events; drafts are reviewable and publish via docs job link (no customer-visible surface change until feature flag enabled).
body:
## Summary
Implements the first version of the Model Changelog Generator worker. The worker consumes model registry change-events, diffs the event payload into a canonical “customer-safe” representation, renders release-note templates, stores a draft changelog entry, and enqueues a docs publish job (linkable from Console/ops tooling).

This PR focuses on the generator worker itself and storage of drafts; it intentionally does not wire the end-to-end approval workflow UI (handled in follow-ups). The output is designed to support the draft -> in_review -> published states, but this PR only creates drafts and attaches the docs publish job reference.

## Motivation / context
Today model changes get communicated via ad-hoc messages, docs updates, and occasional runtime release notes. We’re standardizing on: model registry as source-of-truth + signed change-events -> generator -> customer-visible release notes. This worker is the missing middle step.

This aligns with ENG-4926 and supports support escalations like SUP-18455 where model behavior/metadata drift led to missing/incorrect customer communication.

## What this changes
- Adds `model-changelog-generator-worker` service (worker runtime) that:
  - Subscribes to the `model_registry.change_events.v1` topic
  - Validates event schema and required metadata (schema v1)
  - Computes a normalized diff summary (field-level, with allowlist)
  - Renders a customer-safe draft release note using templating rules
  - Stores the draft entry in `changelog_entries` with status `draft`
  - Enqueues a docs publish job request (no publish is performed in this PR)
  - Emits generator metrics and structured logs (success/failure + publish lag)
- Introduces a public field allowlist for rendering (redacts internal-only metadata by default).
- Adds deterministic ordering for events from the same model/version via `(event_time, event_id)` to avoid draft “flapping” when multiple updates land close together.

## Non-goals
- No automatic “quality delta narrative” from eval diffs (only includes links/metrics placeholders when present).
- No per-customer customized release notes.
- No streaming customer feed; worker runs continuously, but publish targets are batch-oriented.

## Implementation details
### Event consumption
- Uses existing event bus client with at-least-once semantics.
- Idempotency key: `event_id` (stored in `processed_events` table with TTL; additionally enforced via unique constraint on `(event_id)` to prevent duplicate draft creation).
- Retries with exponential backoff on transient DB/doc job enqueue failures.

### Rendering + redaction
- Template selection uses `change_type` derived from diff heuristics:
  - `addition` (new model/version)
  - `update` (metadata changes)
  - `compatibility` (context window, tool/function calling, output format)
  - `performance` (throughput/latency profiles)
  - `deprecation` (sunset date / replacement)
- Only renders fields from `public_changelog_fields` allowlist; everything else is excluded, including internal model nicknames and vendor-specific provenance notes.
- Always includes a Compatibility section (even if “No customer-facing compatibility changes.”) per docs style guidance.

### Storage
- Adds `changelog_entries` table with:
  - `entry_id`, `model_id`, `version_id`, `event_id`, `status`, `customer_safe_summary`, `customer_safe_details`, `links_json`, `created_at`, `updated_at`
  - Note: `links_json` currently stores docs job reference + optional eval dashboard links; approval workflow additions will extend this.

### Docs publish job integration
- Enqueues a request into `docs_publish_jobs` with `job_type=model_changelog_entry` and `entry_id`.
- Worker stores returned `job_id` and includes it in the draft for operator visibility.

### Observability
- Metrics (statsd):
  - `changelog_generator.events_consumed_total{result=ok|error}`
  - `changelog_generator.render_time_ms`
  - `changelog_generator.db_write_time_ms`
  - `changelog_generator.docs_job_enqueue_total{result=ok|error}`
  - `changelog_generator.backlog_age_ms` (based on event timestamp vs process time)
- Tracing: spans around consume -> validate -> diff -> render -> persist -> enqueue.

## Testing
- Unit tests for:
  - schema validation + required field enforcement
  - redaction/allowlist behavior
  - template selection for common change types
  - idempotent processing on duplicate `event_id`
- Integration-ish tests using fixtures for:
  - “new version published” event -> creates draft + docs job
  - “deprecation fields added” event -> includes sunset and replacement fields

## Rollout plan
- Deploy worker in staging with subscription on `model_registry.change_events.v1.staging`.
- Keep production subscription disabled until approval workflow endpoints land.
- Backfill/migration tooling will create synthetic events for older changes in a separate run (not included here).

## Follow-ups
- Approval workflow endpoints + RBAC enforcement for publishing (PR in progress; see ENG-4926/ENG-4932).
- Console surfaces + docs site feed wiring.
- Style linting / template guardrails (docs CI) and publishing backpressure handling.

## Screenshots / sample output
Example draft produced for metadata update (trimmed):
"Summary: Updated compatibility metadata for rw:llama-3-70b-instruct@2026-02-12. Compatibility: No breaking changes; tool calling remains supported. Notes: Added explicit context window and structured output compatibility fields."

---

### Commits
- generator: scaffold worker service + consumer loop
- generator: add diff normalization + change type classification
- generator: render templates + allowlist redaction
- storage: add changelog_entries + processed_events tables and migrations
- docs: add docs_publish_jobs enqueue client + job model
- obs: metrics + tracing + structured logs
- tests: fixtures + unit tests for rendering/idempotency

### Changed areas (high-level)
- services/model-changelog-generator/
- packages/model-registry-events/
- packages/changelog-templates/
- services/docs-publisher-client/
- db/migrations/20260213_add_changelog_entries.sql
- db/migrations/20260213_add_processed_events.sql
- internal/runbooks/model-changelog-generator.md

### Illustrative snippet (redaction/allowlist)
`render_payload = redact(event.payload, allowlist=PUBLIC_CHANGELOG_FIELDS)`
`summary = template.render(change_type, render_payload)`

---

## Review conversation
Jada Williams: Can we guarantee idempotency beyond best-effort? At-least-once delivery means duplicates are common.
Michael Nguyen: Added `processed_events` with unique `(event_id)` and made `(event_id)` unique on `changelog_entries`. Worker treats unique violations as success and continues.

Elliot Price: Please ensure Compatibility is always present and avoid internal terms like "kernel"/"scheduler" in customer_safe_summary.
Michael Nguyen: Updated templates to always include Compatibility section; removed kernel terminology and mapped perf notes to "latency/throughput" language only.

Connor O'Brien: How does this behave during release freeze? We need predictable backlog behavior and a way to pause publish requests.
Michael Nguyen: Worker can be deployed independently of docs publisher; docs job enqueue can be toggled via `GENERATOR_ENQUEUE_DOCS_JOBS=false` and we still store drafts. Added metric `backlog_age_ms` for monitoring.

Logan Wright: Metrics names ok; can you add `result` labels to all counters and ensure no high-cardinality tags (model_id).
Michael Nguyen: Removed model_id as a tag; only logs include model_id/version_id. Added `result` label across counters.

Ethan Park: DB migrations ok, but can we avoid `links_json` being free-form forever?
Michael Nguyen: Agree; using `links_json` as a temporary envelope for docs job + eval links. Follow-up will formalize the schema once approval/publish surfaces are fully defined.

Requested changes addressed:
- Added deterministic ordering using `(event_time, event_id)`
- Added template constraints: always include compatibility, avoid internal terminology
- Reduced metric tag cardinality
